title: Can two decimals multiply to a natural number?
description: Two point five times zero point four and zero point two five times eight are written as fractions and multiplied. The tops and the bottoms are compared to see when the answer is a natural number. Keeko doubts that a decimal times a decimal is never a natural number.
teaching_notes: One idea: a multiplication of decimals gives a natural number when the top of the answer fraction is a multiple of its bottom. Watch for students who think a decimal point in the numbers always leaves a decimal point in the answer.

source: Can the product of two decimals be a natural number? Can the product of a decimal and a natural number be a natural number? Test 2.5 × 0.4 and 0.25 × 8
video_script.why: After multiplying decimals through fractions, the child tests a doubt from the book: can the answer lose its decimal point altogether.
video_script.substitution: the book's two tests, two point five times zero point four and zero point two five times eight
video_script.anchor: Two multiplications from the book, two point five times zero point four and zero point two five times eight, with the question whether the answer can be a natural number
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip says that when a decimal point is in the numbers multiplied, the answer is never a natural number. But the tops multiplied can be a multiple of the bottoms multiplied, and then the point goes away.
video_script.payoff_line: Both questions now have an answer.

final_answer.spoken: yes to both, two point five times zero point four is one and zero point two five times eight is two

maths_rules: a fraction is a natural number when its top is a multiple of its bottom, for example 15/5 = 3
1 and 2 are natural numbers, so a decimal times a decimal, and a decimal times a natural number, can be a natural number
it happens when the product of the tops is a multiple of the product of the bottoms
video_script.design: One idea: a natural number appears when the top is a multiple of the bottom. Assumes the multiplication of decimals as fractions. Wrong idea: decimals never give a natural number. The two multiplications stay all video; the fraction fifteen over five stays through the ground; the values one and two appear only on the answer beat.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>Multiply the tops, twenty five times four. Multiply the bottoms, ten times ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This gives one hundred over one hundred.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>This gives two hundred over one hundred.
